claims.text: ML-assisted thermo-mechanical cycle optimization can concurrently improve strength and ductility in conventional metal alloys.
Optimized processing can produce a refined microstructure with a balanced precipitate distribution.
The proposed method applies to conventional metal alloys with polycrystalline or homogeneous nano-/ultrafine-grained structures.
Machine learning can optimize annealing and deformation cycles.
An annealing treatment of approximately 600°C for 1 hour followed by cold deformation at about 1×10^-3 s^-1 is an appropriate optimized processing cycle.
The processing cycle will improve grain structure.
An ML model can determine nonlinear relationships among processing temperature, time, and deformation rate from experimental and simulation data.
ML analysis can identify a processing window that relieves internal stresses through annealing.
Microstructural refinement and balanced precipitate distribution increase strength.
The proposed combination of annealing and deformation can preserve or improve ductility while increasing strength, avoiding the usual trade-off.
The ML-optimized treatment will increase yield strength or tensile strength relative to conventional processing.
The ML-optimized treatment will increase elongation to failure relative to conventional processing.
Traditional thermo-mechanical processing often exhibits a trade-off in which increased strength is accompanied by reduced ductility.
The approach is expected to be most effective in conventional alloy systems.
The approach may require adjustment or may not be directly applicable to highly complex multiphase or composite materials.
The magnitude of mechanical-property improvement will vary with alloy composition and processing environment.
